round: Who hit the higher top speed?
A burst of speed can decide who reaches a loose puck. Peak speed measures the burst, not the whole race.
A winger who races back to cover an opponent adds distance without touching the puck. Distance also depends on ice time.
A defender in the shooting lane can stop an attempt before it reaches the goalie. A block is not necessarily a goal saved.
A short outlet pass can move a team out of trouble without earning an assist. A count alone cannot show where the puck went.
Who spent longer on the ice?
Time on ice is opportunity. Watch who stays on for an extra shift; the total alone cannot tell you how well they played.
